content.comment_body: When I bought the [product_name] Ethernet version, it came bundled with [product_name] Basic [version_no]. I found a lengthy manual online, but nowhere does it show how to connect with the [product_name]. I've set the IP addresses of both the [product_name] and my PC to be just one digit apart. I can load programs using [product_name] [version_no], but scanning for devices on the LAN yields no results. I can successfully ping the device. Is there a [product_name] specific manual for [product_name]?
Hello [user_name], Please check this link for guidance: How to set up a connection between a [product_name] [article_no] and an HMI Panel? It might help you. Best regards,

Thanks [user_name], I nearly reached this point myself. I planned to run a simulation on the PC for a customer who will use a [version_no] as a master for this [product_name]. I hoped to interact directly with the [product_name] via PC. I need to send a value to the [product_name] at a tag location, which I plan to convert to an analog value, and then read back a converted analog value for the HMI, including any generated alarms. I think I'm confused—do I need an actual HMI to communicate with the [product_name]?

Hello [user_name], I've worked with several [product_name] and HMI connections and would like to assist you! First: To test PC communication with the [product_name], use the "detect" instruction, as shown in step 6 of the referenced link about connecting a [product_name] [article_no] to an HMI Panel. If successful, your PC is communicating with the [product_name]. Second: For [product_name] Basic [version_no]: Use an I/O field to enter values, which will reflect in the [product_name] [product_name] program. Be sure to set up a variable for the I/O field. In [product_name] [product_name], program a network input block, and in its properties, link the address to the variable for the I/O field in your HMI software. This way, values can be modified using other blocks. The linking process is further described in the link above. Let me know if you have additional questions—I'm happy to help! Greetings, [user_name]

I can communicate with the [product_name] using [product_name] [version_no] without any issues and can write and download programs. However, I’m having difficulty setting up the connection between the [product_name] Basic portal and the [product_name]. After speaking to my local supplier, they suggested the device might not appear in scans due to antivirus software. I've set up network IO locations in the [product_name] but can't link to them like you would with a [version_no] device. When I attempt a connection, none of the I/O points on the [product_name] show as available. In the application, under Online and Access Devices, I select PN/IE and my local Ethernet card used by [product_name] [version_no], but the scan returns no devices found. Any ideas? My next step is to try third-party software, like National Instruments, though I expected this to work. Thanks
Hello, Try this attached example (borrowed from [url]). Regards,

Hello [user_name], Try these steps in [product_name] [version_no]: 1. Right-click on Devices & Networks, then right-click the green Ethernet icon and select Add Subnet (unless you've done this already). 2. In Device Configuration, right-click the green Ethernet icon again, go to Properties, and ensure the IP addresses for the HMI, PC, and [product_name] are just one digit apart. 3. In the tag table, check that the acquisition cycle is 100ms and the selected connection matches what you've set up. 4. Right-click the HMI device and select Compile All before attempting to connect. 5. Under Online & Diagnostics, go to PG/PC interface, select PN/IE, and then Go Online. Looking forward to hearing about your progress! Greetings,

I'm trying to use my PC as the HMI. Is this possible with [product_name] Basic [version_no], or do I need an HMI panel or another version of [product_name]? I need to set up a demo for a customer controlling the [product_name] with a [version_no]. When I try to Add Device, only HMI panels appear as options.
Hello, To program HMI runtime directly on your PC, you’ll need [product_name] [version_no] Advanced. Refer to the provided link for more details.

Hello [user_name], You currently have [product_name] Basic, which allows you to program a Basic Panel. For instance, you can select a KTP600 PN. Make the correct connection as described in my earlier link. When your program is ready, you can simulate the panel on your PC. Make sure to correctly set the PG/PC interface (via Control Panel on the PC) and select "S7online -> TCP/IP" (choose your ethernet card). You’ll then be able to simulate the KTP600 panel and communicate with the [product_name] from your PC. Best regards,
Thanks everyone. The I/O is working now, and I’m currently setting up the alarm list.

I'm having issues again with [product_name] Basic [version_no] SP2. I have a program that runs correctly on two laptops, using online simulation. However, when I try to run it on a desktop, communication fails. The IP is set properly, and I can download programs. The test connection works, and transferring the same program (with the key code installed) to another machine still won't simulate. The issue seems related to network—on the simulated screen, PLC values aren't visible, and sending a value results in an error: can't transfer to PLC. Thanks
Hello [user_name], Can you successfully ping the device? Is the PG/PC interface configured correctly? Best regards,
Hi, welcome to the forum! This site is helpful for solving various queries, but currently I cannot provide a comment. Sorry for that—thanks. [url]

My laptop displays the correct line to choose. To set up, go to Control Panel on your PC, then Set PG/PC interface and confirm it is "S7online -> TCP/IP" for your selected ethernet card. On the desktop in the lab, TCP/IP doesn't appear as an option for the installed card. I may try installing an older card to see if that resolves the issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants encounter difficulties when trying to simulate and establish an HMI connection between a [product_name] controller and [product_name] Basic [version_no] software directly on their PC. Documentation lacks clarity for PC-to-[product_name] interactions without a physical HMI panel. Users are uncertain about the software's capabilities, such as whether HMI runtime features are supported in their current version or if an upgrade is necessary. Troubleshooting network connectivity remains a challenge, possibly due to conflicts with third-party or antivirus software or configuration problems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward simulation and connection of an HMI interface to the [product_name] controller directly through PC using [product_name] Basic, with clear documentation and visible [product_name] I/O points readily available in the configuration interface.
